Foes
fōz
n. pl. (enemies; rendering Hebrew tsar, Greek echthros)
Old English fah, hostile. Foe is the sharper, older word for enemy — and Christ puts some of them at the family table.

Biblical Definition

Foes are enemies. Christ quotes Micah when describing the cost of following Him: “a man's foes shall be they of his own household” (Mat 10:36; Mic 7:6). The psalmist testifies, “When the wicked, even mine enemies and my foes, came upon me to eat up my flesh, they stumbled and fell” (Psa 27:2). Acts applies the enthronement psalm to Christ: “until I make thy foes thy footstool” (Act 2:35).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines foe as an enemy; one who entertains personal enmity, hatred, grudge or malice against another; and an enemy in war.

expand to see more

FOE, n. An enemy; one who entertains personal enmity, hatred, grudge or malice, against another.

2. An enemy in war; a hostile army.

3. An opponent; an enemy; one who opposes any thing in principle.

Key Scripture

Mat 10:36 — "And a man's foes shall be they of his own household."

Mic 7:6 — "For the son dishonoureth the father, the daughter riseth up against her mother, the daughter in law against her mother in law; a man's enemies are the men of his own house."

Psa 27:2 — "When the wicked, even mine enemies and my foes, came upon me to eat up my flesh, they stumbled and fell."

Act 2:35 — "Until I make thy foes thy footstool."

Modern Corruption

Following Christ is sold as improving every relationship, and He warned specifically that it would divide some households down the middle.

expand to see more

Matthew 10:34-36 is the passage least likely to appear on a promotional card: think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. For I am come to set a man at variance against his father… and a man's foes shall be they of his own household. Christ is not describing a failure of discipleship but a predictable consequence of it, and He says it so that converts from divided homes will not conclude they have done something wrong.

The comfort follows in the next verses rather than in a denial. He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me — and then, he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it. The cost is stated at full price, and the compensation is stated in the same breath. Micah, whom He quotes, ends the same passage with therefore I will look unto the LORD.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew tsar (H6862), adversary, foe; oyeb (H341), enemy; Greek echthros (G2190), hostile, an enemy.

expand to see more

Hebrew tsar (H6862) — adversary, foe; Psalm 27:2, 44:5, 60:12.

Greek echthros (G2190) — enemy, foe; Matthew 10:36, Acts 2:35, Romans 5:10.

Hebrew oyeb (H341) — enemy; Micah 7:6 in context, Psalm 110:1.

Usage

"“A man's foes shall be they of his own household” — a warning, not a failure."

"“They stumbled and fell” — the psalmist's report of the outcome."

"“Until I make thy foes thy footstool” — the enthronement psalm applied to Christ."
